note: Phase 1 drawing test (2026-10-02), revised the same day after John's review. Read by tools/contact_sheet.py. Credits and licences are in ../research/play-image-plan.json. The failed Iphigenia at Aulis test stays in rejected/ and off the sheet.

drawings.name: Aeschylus · the Pythia (Eumenides)
drawings.alt: The Pythia, Apollo's priestess, fleeing in terror with her hands raised
drawings.source: Bötticher's 1859 drawing of an Apulian krater, Orestes at Delphi (Heidelberg scan, public domain)
drawings.method: Engraved plate: cut along her own lines, with straight cuts across blank paper; Apollo's overlapping foot erased; potrace
drawings.verdict: Clean. Revised: her right arm, the curl on top of her head, her left index finger and the whole shawl (both ends and the black folds) are now in.

drawings.name: Sophocles · Oedipus (before the Sphinx)
drawings.alt: Oedipus, a young traveller in cloak and short tunic, standing with a spear
drawings.source: Achilles Painter pelike, Berlin F 2355, photograph by Gary Todd (CC0)
drawings.method: Red-figure photo: clay found by colour (shiny glaze), fold lines by local contrast, hair outlined by hand, potrace
drawings.verdict: Usable. Revised: every cloak fold and the hat on his back now show. The painter's own drawing is sparer than the engravings; the lower cloak is ragged where the vase is restored.

drawings.name: Euripides · Iphigenia (Iphigenia in Tauris)
drawings.alt: Iphigenia, priestess of Artemis, holding out a letter tablet and the temple key
drawings.source: 1849 lithograph of the Buckingham vase, Archäologische Zeitung Taf. XII (public domain)
drawings.method: Lithograph: lines by local contrast, cut along her own lines, potrace
drawings.verdict: Clean. Revised: her right forearm and key hand are whole. The hand on the tablet stays coarse: this scan shows it about 50px wide.

drawings.name: Aristophanes · Mika (Women at the Thesmophoria)
drawings.alt: Mika, in a comic old woman's mask, holding out a bowl
drawings.source: Würzburg krater H 5697, photograph by ArchaiOptix (CC BY-SA 4.0)
drawings.method: Red-figure photo: clay mask, fold lines by local contrast, Mnesilochus' knife cut away, potrace
drawings.verdict: Clean. Revised: the drapery folds now run their full length. The painter's own drawing is sparer than the engravings.

drawings.name: Medea · in the serpent chariot
drawings.alt: Medea in a chariot drawn by two serpents
drawings.source: Cleveland Museum of Art 1991.1, museum photograph, full-resolution TIFF (CC0)
drawings.method: Red-figure photo: clay mask, disk border cut away, sleeve outlined by hand; lines from the full-resolution TIFF; potrace
drawings.verdict: Usable. Revised: the face (eyelids, pupils, brows, nose, lips, chin) and the diadem now show. Still the busiest drawing.
